cases.customer_question: How should a qualification submission be handled when a referenced QDID uses older ICS definitions that trigger a consistency-check warning?
question_variants: Why is there a yellow warning on Submission Requirement?
Can I submit when the referenced QDID lacks newer ICS items?
What does a TCW do for an ICS consistency warning?
How are older QDIDs treated by the current consistency checker?
Can a submission proceed despite missing ICS fields in an included design?
cases.actual_issue: The referenced qualification was created using an older ICS definition set that contains fewer ICS items than the current qualification system. The current consistency checker flags missing items and generates a submission warning requiring TCW handling.
cases.plain_english_explanation: Older Bluetooth qualifications may not contain all of the fields used by the current qualification tools. When the system compares the old qualification against current rules, it can generate warnings even though the design itself is still being reused. A Test Case Waiver process is used to allow the submission to proceed when the warning matches an approved condition.
cases.consultant_answer: The warning was caused by differences between the older ICS definitions used by the referenced QDID and the current ICS model used by the qualification system. When the consistency checker identifies only items that do not exist in the referenced QDID's original ICS and therefore evaluates them as unsupported, the submission can proceed using the applicable TCW. The submission is then reviewed by Bluetooth SIG administrators before final approval.
cases.decision_logic: The issue is not a functional design inconsistency but a qualification-tool mismatch between historical and current ICS definitions. An approved TCW allows the submission to proceed when the detected inconsistency falls within the waiver's scope.
cases.final_recommendation: Document the applicable TCW in the submission, proceed with submission review, and await Bluetooth SIG approval of the waiver condition before considering the registration complete.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Failure to recognize the warning as a TCW-eligible historical ICS mismatch could lead to unnecessary investigation, qualification rework, or delays in submission approval.
